svg.title: Drawbridge — Review timeline
svg.text: AI writing SaaS · processes customer text · ~$40k/yr · contact leah@nimbuswrite.ai
Tiered as Tier 1 — processes customer data and is an AI service. Plan checkpointed: 7 steps.
P1 blocked — outbound email requires a human approval token. Review parked, scope contact.
Priya Raman authorised first contact. Single-use token issued, expires in 24h.
60 questions sent, tailored from bank.yaml. idem_key rev_7f3a91:questionnaire_send:v1
Reply 1 of 3 parsed — 22 answers merged, mean confidence 0.91. 2 queued for Priya.
SOC 2 Type II report screened — clean. Promoted to evidence-clean, stamped.
Reconcile the vendor's questionnaire claims against their own audit evidence.
Vendor claims MFA enforced org-wide (Q14). SOC 2 exception note 3.2 records an unremediated
MFA gap for administrative access. Flagged access_control, severity high, contradiction
No prior reviews for this vendor.
Org policy recalled: we always require SOC 2 Type II
for processors of customer data. Applied at tiering.
One vertical stream, not a dashboard of
A review is a story that happened over days. The
timeline is the product's core metaphor and the screen
the demo lives on — everything else is a panel beside
Every entry expands to goal, decision,
This is the OpenTelemetry span rendered as prose. It
makes the reasoning auditable in the UI, and it is the
same data the binder prints. Show it expanding on
Memory Bank gets its own panel
L3 is invisible unless you draw it. On a second review
of the same vendor this panel fills with prior history
— the payoff shot for the memory-hierarchy claim.
Screening verdict sits on every document
Not a security page somewhere else. The clean/blocked
verdict belongs beside the file it describes, so the
defence is visible even when nothing is wrong.
